name: Barnabas
summary: A Levite from Cyprus named Joses, whom the apostles called Barnabas, meaning son of consolation. He stood up for Saul, encouraged the new church at Antioch, and travelled with Paul preaching to the Gentiles.

key_moments.title: Giving Away His Land
key_moments.description: Joses, a Levite from Cyprus whom the apostles named Barnabas, sold his land and brought the money to the apostles. The believers shared like this so that no one among them was in need.

key_moments.title: Standing Up for Saul
key_moments.description: When Saul came to Jerusalem, the disciples were afraid of him and did not believe he was a disciple. Barnabas brought him to the apostles and told how Saul had seen the Lord and had spoken boldly in Damascus in Jesus' name.

key_moments.title: Sent to Antioch
key_moments.description: The church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to Antioch, where he was glad to see God's grace at work and urged the believers to hold fast to the Lord. He fetched Saul from Tarsus, they taught there for a whole year, and the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.

key_moments.title: Mistaken for a God
key_moments.description: At Lystra, after Paul healed a man who had never walked, the crowd called Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercurius and wanted to offer sacrifices to them. Barnabas and Paul tore their clothes and cried out that they were only men.

key_moments.title: Parting from Paul
key_moments.description: Barnabas wanted to take John Mark on their next journey, but Paul did not, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia. Their quarrel grew so sharp that they parted, and Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.
